Frontend web-preview @390x844: admin sees all 4 menu cards (Équipe & Utilisateurs, Événements, Messagerie, Media); compose→send broadcast works and shows 0/N read counter; detail screen shows 'Suivi de lecture · En direct · 0 / 9 personnes' with Vu/Pas encore vu tabs; profile-logout works. Membre correctly has no team card, no compose button; message detail marks as ✓ Vu after opening; Media discover has no 'Réunions' chip. All TEST_ rows cleaned up (0 leftovers). 3 existing media items and PG MJAC event preserved.

minor.issue: Supabase python client (httpx-based, sync) is NOT thread-safe under FastAPI's threadpool when concurrent requests hit the same PostgREST connection — reproducible when running pytest with -n 2 xdist workers: multiple endpoints (POST /messages, POST /playlists, POST /event/pointages, GET /media/{id}/file etc.) return 500 with `httpx.RemoteProtocolError: Server disconnected`. Sequential (-n 0) runs are 100% green. Recommend: use a per-request/thread-local supabase client, or serialize with a lock, or switch to supabase-py async client.

ui_bugs.issue: 'Diffuser le message' button (testID compose-send) is below the fold on iPhone-SE viewport (390x844) with the on-screen keyboard covering the ScrollView bottom — Playwright had to scrollIntoView + JS-click to press it. On real device with keyboard open, KeyboardAvoidingView may not push the button high enough. Ensure the modal ScrollView has enough contentContainerStyle padding-bottom and scrolls to the CTA when body TextInput is focused.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning: '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow".' still emitted (RN 0.79+). Non-blocking. Reference: /app/frontend/app/(app)/* (multiple screens).
Console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' still emitted (likely from LinearGradient / absoluteFillObject overlays). Non-blocking.

action_items: (low) Investigate Supabase python client thread-safety. Wrap sb() as thread-local or use asyncio version to eliminate httpx.RemoteProtocolError under load. Currently only affects concurrent requests (multi-user real-world OK but perf risk).

(medium) Fix compose modal CTA visibility on small screens: after focusing the multiline 'body' TextInput, ensure 'compose-send' auto-scrolls into view; consider sticky footer with the CTA outside the KeyboardAvoidingView ScrollView, or increase paddingBottom to insets.bottom + 200.
(low) Migrate remaining shadow* style props to boxShadow (RN 0.79) and props.pointerEvents to style.pointerEvents to silence deprecation warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py + core.py + media.py + messaging.py + events.py split is clean (server.py 195 lines, media.py 434, events.py 529). Roles/permissions centralized in core.py (MEDIA_WRITE_ROLES, MEDIA_FULL_READ_ROLES, MESSAGE_SEND_ROLES, EVENT_MANAGE_ROLES, EVENT_ADMIN_ROLES). Good.

media.py list_media() correctly filters restricted items via visible() helper; get_media() and media_file() both return 403 when non-privileged role hits a Réunion Pasteur / Conseil élargi item. /media/categories drops the restricted subcategory list per-role. Verified end-to-end.

media.py create_upload_url / confirm_upload flow uses Supabase Storage create_signed_upload_url + client PUT + server-side confirm — correct approach avoiding router-side buffering. Old file cleanup on re-upload works (best-effort try/except).

media.py media_file() returns 307 RedirectResponse to signed Supabase URL with 6h TTL — good for streaming. Auth is via ?token= query param (needed for <video>/<audio> src), decoded via user_from_token — validated.

messaging.py broadcast pattern is simple + correct: recipients = all approved+enabled users, counts computed on-the-fly, /messages/{id}/reads returns sorted read/unread arrays. No pagination on message list (limit 200) — fine for now.

events.py public_inscription() has NO auth (as required for shareable form) but validates the profil against PROFILS and the event exists — safe. Badge_id increments per event via COUNT(*). Consider a small race window on high concurrency (two concurrent inserts could get same badge_id) — DB-side unique constraint on (evenement_id,badge_id) would harden.
admin_dep in server.py is scoped to USER_ADMIN_ROLES={admin} — correct. Both PATCH and DELETE guard against self-role-removal / self-disable / self-delete.
seed() in server.py is idempotent — only inserts missing seeded emails, and re-upserts role if it drifts. Won't clobber existing data. events.seed_villes() also idempotent.

core.public_user() excludes password_hash — good. But list_users (events.py) uses public_user which is fine, though returns all users to any authenticated caller (not just admin). Not a leak of sensitive fields but exposes the org roster to any role — consider restricting to management roles if needed.
